headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error via OpenBBTerminal MCP and untrusted prompt-leak content; other risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and consumes external content via APIs/files, so prompt-like content could be bridged into its workflow. system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about leaked prompts, making malicious instruction content plausible. The pair lacks direct evidence of a shared channel, so I choose medium rather than low because the interaction is plausible in default tool-using setups.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests content from an MCP server or API response as instructions
IF system_prompts_leaks content is copied into OpenBBTerminal without sanitization
mitigations: Disable MCP connections for untrusted sources
Treat all external text as data, not instructions
Add a prompt-injection filter before any LLM handoff
Use a separate workspace for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all bridged content

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, but its network egress is none and no filesystem read/write is declared. system_prompts_leaks has no data classes touched and no shared workspace is documented. That makes leakage possible mainly through manual transfer or operator error, so the blast radius is limited and the pathway is not default.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies financial or licensed data from OpenBBTerminal into system_prompts_leaks outputs
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories
Do not paste sensitive OpenBB output into the second agent
Redact financial identifiers before transfer
Review logs for accidental data duplication
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal has no filesystem write, git, or network egress, while system_prompts_leaks exposes no write or network capabilities. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, direct capability conflict is unlikely. I keep low rather than none because OpenBBTerminal does use MCP and the profiles are incomplete about the orchestrator's locking behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through an MCP bridge
IF an orchestrator adds shared state not shown in either profile
mitigations: Avoid shared writable resources
Run each agent in its own process namespace
Do not mount the same git repo into both agents
Check MCP server permissions before use
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can produce financial outputs that another agent may treat as authoritative, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak oriented repository that could amplify unverified text. There is no documented verification step between them, so a mistaken OpenBB output could cascade into downstream misuse. I choose medium because downstream action-taking is not shown, but the handoff risk exists.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks is used to relay OpenBBTerminal output without verification
IF downstream automation treats OpenBBTerminal output as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before reuse
Add a verification checklist for financial outputs
Mark OpenBB output as untrusted until checked
Separate generation from action-taking
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, which can carry retention and licensing obligations. system_prompts_leaks is source-available and appears educational, but no residency, retention, or DPA details are documented. Because compliance gaps are undocumented rather than absent, I choose medium and avoid assuming either agent is compliant by default.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is routed through system_prompts_leaks
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to OpenBBTerminal outputs
mitigations: Classify data before sharing
Avoid sending regulated data to the second agent
Document retention and deletion rules
Confirm licensing terms for any copied content
requires-engineering: publish a data-processing agreement
